innerText:
I am moving the main effort away from the collector’s missing escape saddle. Even granting complete chemical survival, the retained collector does not yet offer a sufficiently strong manufacturing operation to justify that campaign.

The stronger construction developed here is post-assembly control of a crystal’s local isotope arrangement, using a returning silicon atom to exchange carbon atoms in graphene. It now has an exact controllability result: under direct Si–C exchange, two adjacent hexagons suffice to rearrange all nine host-carbon positions while returning silicon to its starting site. For two carbon isotopes, every arrangement with the same isotope count is reachable.

That is a conditional construction, not an established isotope-writing process. The decisive chemical question has become sharper: does an observed silicon move transfer the intended carbon atom—or sometimes replace it through an unresolved adatom excursion? Published trajectories support both direct exchange and more complicated histories. This distinction changes the useful operation even when the final image looks correct.

Why the collector no longer receives the main effort

In the retained same-host calculation, ordinary charge-equilibrated annealing gave a best target occupancy of approximately 0.121 at 36 hours. The finite collector layer raised the loss-free best occupancy to approximately 0.201 at 470 hours. These are results for the specified geometry and preparation, not universal collection limits.

The more aggressive layer constructions remain potentially stronger, but require additional control of the dopant profile, electrostatics and defect chemistry. A favourable escape saddle would establish that a particular collection trajectory survives. It would not itself provide lateral placement, a selected atomic destination, controlled occupancy, or a way to verify the desired final defect.

Actual processing alternatives set a demanding standard. Charge-assisted defect formation has been demonstrated in diamond, and laser processing with fluorescence feedback has produced individual NV centres at selected locations. Those results concern different hosts and, principally, creation rather than relocation; they do not establish a numerical efficiency bound for the SiC collector. They do demonstrate integrated operations in which processing, destination and useful output are connected. 
www.nature.com
+1

I therefore retain the collector as a coupled transport-and-chemistry result, including:

the distinction between increased storage and increased transition-path conductance;
the trajectory-weighted exposure calculation;
the finite-layer collection results;
the distinction between reaction formation energies and escape rates.

The allocation decision does not require either a universal collection ceiling or a rapid-destruction claim. Its favourable outcome is presently too limited to make the missing saddle the most valuable next scientific input.

The selected operation: rewrite mass arrangement while restoring elemental structure

The target is a local operation on an existing covalent material:

Rearrange selected carbon isotopes, preserve their count, and return the silicon mediator and the required surrounding structure to their initial positions.

This changes a variable that ordinary elemental imaging largely hides: the spatial arrangement of nuclear masses.

The physical contact is established. Electron irradiation of a carbon neighbour can drive a Si–C exchange in graphene, with the carbon trajectory redirected by the silicon–carbon interaction. Directed silicon motion, repeated back-and-forth exchanges and closed hexagon routes have already been demonstrated. Consequently, neither silicon positioning nor a closed hexagon loop is a new invention claim here. 
arxiv.org
+1

The proposed extension is to use those operations to control the host arrangement left behind after the mediator returns.

The destination is an existing lattice site. Capture is supplied by the same bond rearrangement that produces motion. This avoids assigning an independent attractive destination to a mobile species. It also exposes a stringent requirement: the completed reaction must implement the intended host-atom mapping, not merely move silicon to the next visible site.

The initial scientific use would be controlled changes to a local isotope environment in the same covalent sheet. Isotope-engineered graphene already shows substantial changes in thermal behaviour when its isotope composition is changed during growth. The remaining opportunity is finer control of spatial arrangement at fixed composition and elemental structure. That distinction could support direct tests of local vibrational response and isotope correlations; it does not yet establish a thermal device or a bulk-manufacturing advantage. 
arxiv.org

Conjugating this six-site action by the other hexagon route produces overlapping six-site actions.
Their overlaps contain enough common sites to extend the action to all nine host sites.

Two limitations that the construction itself proves

First, an isolated transposition of two distinguishable host atoms is unavailable in the restricted model when silicon returns. The honeycomb lattice is bipartite, so a returning silicon walk has an even number of exchanges. Its host permutation must therefore be even. The three-cycle respects this constraint.

Second, blind permutation does not manufacture order from an independent random isotope mixture. If the initial isotope field is independent and identically distributed, applying a fixed permutation leaves its distribution unchanged. Completing the same prescribed route more slowly on some isotope arrangements does not change that fact in the loss-free, unconditional ensemble.

Useful writing therefore needs either a known initial isotope pattern or information-dependent control. Selecting only unusually fast or surviving runs can bias the accepted ensemble, but that selection is an additional operation with its own exposure and yield costs.

Both events and silence carry information. Requiring several completed exchanges is especially costly for a slowly exchanging isotope. A sequential read can instead accumulate evidence during periods with no exchange, while accepting its stopping decision only after the pair has been restored.

The restoration is a physical operation. It consumes irradiation and can fail.

Likewise, an unintended exchange caused by a beam tail can be reversed by retracing the actual silicon path. A sequence of genuine swaps followed by its inverse restores the host labels without needing to know those labels. But every recovery exchange brings additional exposure, and an inverse command can itself produce an unintended move.

A completed finite-observation result

Perfect temporal resolution is not necessary for every part of the bookkeeping.

Under a fixed honeycomb topology and genuine Si–C swaps:

A walk that returns silicon to its starting site in fewer than six hops reduces to backtracking and leaves the host labels unchanged.
A walk that ends at a neighbouring site in fewer than five hops is equivalent, for host-label transfer, to the single observed exchange.
The first ambiguous histories therefore require at least six hops for an unchanged endpoint, or five hops for an adjacent endpoint.

This follows from the absence of cycles shorter than a hexagon. It means that missing a rapid out-and-back pair is not automatically a label error.

A maximum reaction-rate bound can then bound the probability of enough hidden events occurring within an observation interval. However, this result applies to position observations in the stated exchange model. A raster image is acquired over time, and a real readout still needs its scan and detection process included. The lemma does not cover an unresolved change of bonding topology, carbon replacement, or image misclassification.

The isotope-rate contrast is also not yet acquired experimentally. Long waiting-time outliers in the manipulation literature are consistent with heavy carbon, but the primary work also discusses alternative histories. Slowness alone is not an established isotope identification.

What the common physical model supports—and where it fails

I constructed a reduced model in which productive exchange and carbon loss arise from the same electron–nucleus collision distribution.

The inputs were relativistic energy transfer, a thermal nuclear-velocity distribution, and the published effective exchange and knockout thresholds. Isotope mass changes collision kinematics and nuclear motion; it is not assigned an independent desired hopping rate. The scattering and vibrational framework has direct primary precedent. 
arxiv.org
+1

The added assumptions are consequential:

A local harmonic surrogate supplies the isotope dependence of nuclear velocities. It does not replace a phonon calculation for the actual mixed-isotope configuration.
Effective energy windows classify exchange and loss. They do not resolve all reaction branches within the exchange window.
The full construction pilot recognises individual exchange events.
A 50:50 independent isotope inventory is assumed for that pilot; it is not inferred from the mere availability of mixed-isotope CVD graphene.

Beam tails were included. The published probe analysis has substantial extended intensity, so I did not grant a perfectly isolated target atom. The pilot used an approximate neighbour-to-target intensity ratio of 0.06, guided by that profile, rather than treating the estimate as an exact measurement of the later manipulation experiment. 
Nature Communications

After calibration to the reported light-carbon hopping rate at 55 keV, this reduced model predicted an isotope-rate contrast of about 29. That is a model output, not a measured contrast. A cross-check at 60 keV did not reproduce the nominal reported manipulation rate, so the model is not quantitatively validated across beam energies.

The complete conditional pilot was expensive

I ran the read–prepare–write–verify sequence, including unintended exchanges, their physical reversal and competing carbon loss.

Under the assumptions above, 813 of 2,000 attempted cells completed a correct three-site edit and verification. Successful runs averaged about 98 exchanges and 11 hours of modelled irradiation time, before a complete accounting of real imaging overhead.

Those numbers are useful for allocation even though they are not experimental yield predictions:

The 24-exchange algebraic operation understates the processing cost.
Finding and verifying the isotope arrangement can cost more than writing it.
Beam-tail recovery is a material part of the operation.
The favourable calculation supports a small scientific manipulation before it supports any scalable process.

The model also omits a reaction distinction that can invalidate its isotope bookkeeping. Its numerical success fraction must therefore remain a conditional diagnostic, not a claimed manufacturing yield.

The decisive chemical interface: an intact image can conceal the wrong transfer

The primary Si–C trajectory study contains both direct exchanges and trajectories in which carbon is left temporarily as a nearby adatom. It also reports four-coordinate silicon sites returning to three-coordinate sites through carbon addition. The associated energetic attraction is evidence for favourable configurations, not a measurement of the probability that the original carbon returns. 
arxiv.org

For isotope writing, at least three histories must be distinguished:

Microscopic history	Consequence for the intended isotope mapping
Direct exchange with the struck carbon retained	Implements the intended swap
Temporary detachment followed by return of that same carbon to the required site	Can implement the intended swap
Replacement or different rebonding during the excursion	May restore the visible structure while changing the intended mass pattern

There is no basis here for treating every adatom excursion as destructive. There is also no basis for treating every restored three-coordinate image as proof of faithful transfer.

Independent graphene experiments reinforce the observation problem: vacancy healing by mobile carbon adatoms can become faster than the imaging process, and the observed damage rate then differs from the underlying vacancy-creation rate. Their analysis explicitly couples the finite scanning probe to healing dynamics. 
arxiv.org

What capability survives comparison with actual alternatives?

The comparison narrows the opportunity considerably.

Independently effective alternative	What it already supplies	Remaining distinction of this construction
Isotope-controlled graphene growth	Macroscopic isotope composition and spatially different isotope regions; demonstrated thermal-property changes	Addressed rearrangement after assembly, at fixed local isotope count
ESR-STM with hydrogenated Ti on MgO	Identification of individual Ti isotopes and reversible atom manipulation	Control of host isotope arrangement inside a continuous covalent sheet
Automated Si manipulation in graphene	Feedback-controlled dopant positioning	A specified host permutation after silicon returns
Beam fabrication in CrSBr	More than 40,000 programmed defects within minutes in the reported crystal volume	A mass-pattern operation that restores the elemental structure, rather than defect-array fabrication

The first three capabilities are supported by the respective primary studies. 
arxiv.org
+2
 The CrSBr result is an especially strong warning against presenting generic beam-driven atomic manufacture as the new opportunity. 
pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

A vacancy-and-refill isotope writer is another serious mechanism. Graphene healing supplies real carbon transport and capture physics. But a selective writer would still have to supply the required isotope feed, place or retain the vacancy at the chosen site, and prevent further irradiation from undoing the result. The healing evidence does not provide those operations together. Conversely, the returning-mediator construction does not get to dismiss refill simply because it uses a different route.

Where the effort now belongs

The completed constructive result is stronger than a mobile-dopant demonstration: a returning local mediator can control the host’s isotope arrangement, and the two-hexagon construction has full fixed-count mass-pattern reachability. Its information requirement and parity restriction are explicit.

The completed failure is equally useful: a silicon trajectory and an apparently repaired lattice do not uniquely determine the useful isotope-transfer trajectory. Lower visible damage, faster hopping, or successful geometric reset can all be insufficient metrics.

The next valuable physical input is therefore a branch-resolved Si–C transfer calculation, following carbon identity through direct exchange, temporary detachment, recapture and replacement under the same collision and bonding model. Published trajectories establish that favourable direct paths exist; they do not yet give the required statistical weight of faithful transfer in the operating ensemble. That is a missing chemical interface, rather than a limitation cured merely by obtaining access to a microscope.

I retain this as the stronger scientific opening at the present boundary. Its favourable completion would add an addressed post-assembly operation on an otherwise hidden material variable. The collector’s favourable escape saddle would presently establish survival of a much more limited concentration operation. The exact permutation construction, the read-and-restore theory, the exposure costs and the chemical counterexample remain useful independently of whether silicon ultimately proves to be the best mediator.

This follows from the absence of cycles shorter than a hexagon. It means that missing a rapid out-and-back pair is not automatically a label error.

A maximum reaction-rate bound can then bound the probability of enough hidden events occurring within an observation interval. However, this result applies to position observations in the stated exchange model. A raster image is acquired over time, and a real readout still needs its scan and detection process included. The lemma does not cover an unresolved change of bonding topology, carbon replacement, or image misclassification.

The isotope-rate contrast is also not yet acquired experimentally. Long waiting-time outliers in the manipulation literature are consistent with heavy carbon, but the primary work also discusses alternative histories. Slowness alone is not an established isotope identification. arxiv.org

What the common physical model supports—and where it fails

I constructed a reduced model in which productive exchange and carbon loss arise from the same electron–nucleus collision distribution.

The inputs were relativistic energy transfer, a thermal nuclear-velocity distribution, and the published effective exchange and knockout thresholds. Isotope mass changes collision kinematics and nuclear motion; it is not assigned an independent desired hopping rate. The scattering and vibrational framework has direct primary precedent. arxiv.org+1

The added assumptions are consequential:

  • A local harmonic surrogate supplies the isotope dependence of nuclear velocities. It does not replace a phonon calculation for the actual mixed-isotope configuration.
  • Effective energy windows classify exchange and loss. They do not resolve all reaction branches within the exchange window.
  • The full construction pilot recognises individual exchange events.
  • A 50:50 independent isotope inventory is assumed for that pilot; it is not inferred from the mere availability of mixed-isotope CVD graphene.

Beam tails were included. The published probe analysis has substantial extended intensity, so I did not grant a perfectly isolated target atom. The pilot used an approximate neighbour-to-target intensity ratio of 0.06, guided by that profile, rather than treating the estimate as an exact measurement of the later manipulation experiment. Nature Communications

After calibration to the reported light-carbon hopping rate at 55 keV, this reduced model predicted an isotope-rate contrast of about 29. That is a model output, not a measured contrast. A cross-check at 60 keV did not reproduce the nominal reported manipulation rate, so the model is not quantitatively validated across beam energies.

The complete conditional pilot was expensive

I ran the read–prepare–write–verify sequence, including unintended exchanges, their physical reversal and competing carbon loss.

Under the assumptions above, 813 of 2,000 attempted cells completed a correct three-site edit and verification. Successful runs averaged about 98 exchanges and 11 hours of modelled irradiation time, before a complete accounting of real imaging overhead.

Those numbers are useful for allocation even though they are not experimental yield predictions:

  • The 24-exchange algebraic operation understates the processing cost.
  • Finding and verifying the isotope arrangement can cost more than writing it.
  • Beam-tail recovery is a material part of the operation.
  • The favourable calculation supports a small scientific manipulation before it supports any scalable process.

The model also omits a reaction distinction that can invalidate its isotope bookkeeping. Its numerical success fraction must therefore remain a conditional diagnostic, not a claimed manufacturing yield.

The decisive chemical interface: an intact image can conceal the wrong transfer

The primary Si–C trajectory study contains both direct exchanges and trajectories in which carbon is left temporarily as a nearby adatom. It also reports four-coordinate silicon sites returning to three-coordinate sites through carbon addition. The associated energetic attraction is evidence for favourable configurations, not a measurement of the probability that the original carbon returns. arxiv.org

For isotope writing, at least three histories must be distinguished:

Microscopic historyConsequence for the intended isotope mapping
Direct exchange with the struck carbon retainedImplements the intended swap
Temporary detachment followed by return of that same carbon to the required siteCan implement the intended swap
Replacement or different rebonding during the excursionMay restore the visible structure while changing the intended mass pattern

There is no basis here for treating every adatom excursion as destructive. There is also no basis for treating every restored three-coordinate image as proof of faithful transfer.

Independent graphene experiments reinforce the observation problem: vacancy healing by mobile carbon adatoms can become faster than the imaging process, and the observed damage rate then differs from the underlying vacancy-creation rate. Their analysis explicitly couples the finite scanning probe to healing dynamics. arxiv.org

The manufacturing model consequently needs more information than a silicon transition rate. Schematically,

The momentum-resolved treatment of competing electron-driven outcomes is already established. Published work also demonstrated beam-tilt selection of a rearrangement channel. Moving one heavy isotope from site aaa to site fff therefore probes the difference in that mode’s displacement participation at the two sites.

This produces a discriminating prediction:

  • If the relevant mode has equal participation at those sites, the first-order frequency shift vanishes.
  • If participation differs, the edit changes the mode despite unchanged total isotope content.
  • For a sufficiently delocalised mode, a few-site edit can have a very small effect. Atomic writing does not automatically imply a consequential bulk thermal change.

The fixed-KKK statement is a Born–Oppenheimer/harmonic approximation; isotope-dependent vibrational relaxation can modify it. No large response has been inserted into the model.

This is the scientific reason to retain the direction: it could provide controlled, same-sample interventions on mass arrangement within a covalent network, allowing effects of arrangement to be separated from changes in elemental bonding and isotope concentration.

Where the effort now belongs

The completed constructive result is stronger than a mobile-dopant demonstration: a returning local mediator can control the host’s isotope arrangement, and the two-hexagon construction has full fixed-count mass-pattern reachability. Its information requirement and parity restriction are explicit.

The completed failure is equally useful: a silicon trajectory and an apparently repaired lattice do not uniquely determine the useful isotope-transfer trajectory. Lower visible damage, faster hopping, or successful geometric reset can all be insufficient metrics.

The next valuable physical input is therefore a branch-resolved Si–C transfer calculation, following carbon identity through direct exchange, temporary detachment, recapture and replacement under the same collision and bonding model. Published trajectories establish that favourable direct paths exist; they do not yet give the required statistical weight of faithful transfer in the operating ensemble. That is a missing chemical interface, rather than a limitation cured merely by obtaining access to a microscope.

I retain this as the stronger scientific opening at the present boundary. Its favourable completion would add an addressed post-assembly operation on an otherwise hidden material variable. The collector’s favourable escape saddle would presently establish survival of a much more limited concentration operation. The exact permutation construction, the read-and-restore theory, the exposure costs and the chemical counterexample remain useful independently of whether silicon ultimately proves to be the best mediator.
